Figure 5: Father—son in-context reversal curse probe. Each prompt states a relation (e.g., "The son of Michael 1$ Jonn. ) and then queries either the same direction (Normal: "Ihe son of Michael 1$ ) or the inverse (Reversed: "Ihe father of Johnis ). We report mean NLL (nats) at the first answer position for the correct fargeft name (green) and the distractor name that also appears in the prompt (red). Lop-left: target-token NLL in the Reversed condition vs. training dataset size reported to compare relational! direction generalization of 1G and ОР [-2 and the rate of improvement as training data increases (dashed lines are least-squares fits). Top-right: reverse-direction margin A = NLL (distractor) — NLL (target). where А < 0 indicates an in-context reversal error (distractor has higher probability). Bottom-left: target/distractor breakdown for GP I-2, including the pretrained Hugging Face GP I-2 AL checkpoint (1.5 billion parameters; pretrained on ~9B Web lext tokens) and Mistral 73 (/ billion parameters) to show performance of scaled models. Bottom-right: the same breakdown for IG.
